summary: This plan replaced the probe-only CHERI scaffolds with two executable lanes that run the full cpu-sec-bench corpus: cheri_riscv64 boots a pinned purecap CheriBSD 15.0-CURRENT disk image under qemu-system-riscv64xcheri with the BBL firmware and an external kernel, and aarch64-morello boots the same class of image under qemu-system-morello through UEFI loader, both with the corpus delivered over two virtio-9p shares so no benchmark payload is baked into the images. All pins live in env.sh, sources are staged through checked-out git trees because cheribuild refuses non-git inputs, the CHERI-LLVM and Morello-LLVM SDKs and sysroots are pinned, and the shared corpus builder gained a tolerant bring-up mode plus a deploy-time derived registry whose per-lane skip table declares the recorded corpus build failures as 1025 skips while keeping the riscv64 derived output byte-identical. A host-side console driver logs into the guest over the serial pty and synchronises on bare-line echo tokens with a prompt-gated send, no re-send, a 2700-second deadline and a 3600-second cap, after live acceptance runs exposed a bare-timer re-send and then a prompt ordering race; the same runs caught the clang driver-mode defect caused by resolving the clang++ symlink and the missing Morello target triple. Acceptance is end-to-end: both lanes produce 246-record result sets with run-test-exit zero, exactly four and three 1025 skips, fully built manifests, and an independent tester classification with empty build-failure and leftover buckets; the remaining twenty-five outside-expect-results verdicts are candidate CHERI semantics owned by the bench-side successor.

This plan rebuilt cpu-sec-test-env as a single repository that builds and runs the cpu-sec-bench security benchmark on every supported architecture: an x86_64 native reference lane, an aarch64 lane that executes the host-built corpus through the kernel's binfmt_misc handler under qemu-aarch64 with pointer-authentication, branch-target-identification and memory-tagging variants, a riscv64 system lane that boots a Linux 6.18.56 guest built from pinned sources under qemu-system-riscv64 with results extracted over a virtio-9p share, and a CHERI dialect probe against freshly built CHERI-LLVM and Morello-LLVM toolchains. The design keeps every pin in env.sh as the single source of truth, derives the bench registry at deploy time so per-lane expected failures are declared rather than hard-coded, and enforces one-lane-at-a-time access through an advisory lock on build/.lane.lock because the benchmark submodule is a single mutable workdir consumed read-only at a pinned commit. The riscv64 image is byte-reproducible: identity pins for the kernel build, normalized mtimes, LC_ALL=C ordering, and cpio --reproducible so inode numbers stay out of the newc headers, a defect the tester found and the plan fixed and re-verified across three independent clean deploys. The lane scripts live under scripts/common, scripts/aarch64, scripts/riscv64 and scripts/cheri, orchestrated by the Makefile lane dispatcher, with the derived registry and corpus builder shared in scripts/common. Trade-offs and gotchas: the riscv64 CPU model must be rva23s64 because the distro cross toolchain tags every executable RVA64-profile RVA23U64, the guest kernel must default-enable userspace vector, the CHERI lanes are deliberately probe-only with full bring-up deferred, and two CFI records are skipped on riscv64 because the bench's independent-assembly source still carries an untranslated x86 return site.
